Flex.revenue_growth: CPI $2.2B (+35% YoY), 9.7% op margin; total revenue $7.9B (+21%), op profit $534M
Flex.backlog_or_b2b: EPC'S 2027 IS ALREADY BOOKED, AND A JULY GRID EVENT IS PULLING DEMAND FORWARD (Chris): asked what drives EPC's growth, 'It is all pinned to the data centers. It is all pinned to some of those regulatory requirements that are coming. There is also some tailwinds from bans on foreign-produced product in the critical infrastructure here in the U.S. EPC is all U.S.-based production, so that plays in very well.' Asked about visibility: 'Most of that business is booked today' and 'Really good backlog for 2027.' A specific catalyst was named: 'There was a pretty significant power disturbance in Northern Virginia back in the month of July, and that is driving more utilities to demand this type of technology in the data center.' Margin uplift is attributed to capacity that 'just came online in the month of June', supply-chain reshoring initiatives, and the fact that 'data center margins are a little bit higher than what their traditional business has been.'
Flex.supply_status: Q1 capex $235M (~3% of revenue); FY27 capex $1.5-1.6B for CPI facilities/cooling capacity
Flex.next_catalyst: 400V programs ramping now, 800V next, solid-state after; component constraints already planned into the guide

The consequences are coordination across multiple factories rather than component shortage, and timing variability - is revenue recognized this day or maybe four days later because some of the components are converging in the integration factory. Integration at this scale is a different capability than the power-module integration Vertiv has done for 25, 30 years, and that integration capacity is being deployed constantly to follow demand. He adds the current outlook already incorporates wiggle room against possible hiccups. Chamberlin separately points back to the ramp in infrastructure-solutions orders (Vertiv SmartRun / Vertiv OneCore) seen in last fourth quarter as evidence of the share gain.

On wide-bandgap devices (silicon carbide, gallium nitride) Delta works early and closely with the most important suppliers, keeps talking with them continuously and gets early access to new products, but will not disclose any agreements; it is also broadening its supply chain, including Taiwanese supplier options. Supplier price increases will be negotiated and passed to customers where the business model allows, with a timing lag.

With advanced packaging work flowing to Taiwan OSATs, which are accelerating capex, Tazmo is receiving inquiries and orders from Taiwan OSATs for debond cleaners and coater/developers. The large Q2 coater/developer order came from a limited number of Taiwan OSATs, building on Tazmo's continued deliveries to them; management infers two drivers: rising conventional wafer-level packaging demand (PCs, tablets) and part of the advanced-packaging process moving from a Taiwan foundry to OSATs, in steps that appear to use Tazmo's coater/developers. Coater/developer margins are not expected to differ much from debond cleaners, with clear volume benefits. For 2027, current orders deliver and are booked as sales next year, so order intake is expected to settle somewhat; management does not currently expect the current high order value to continue as is.
Tazmo.supply_status: Capacity roadmap, management (results briefing Q&A): units, modules and parts machining are being expanded through the TAZMO VIETNAM plant expansion and added staff, with the Vietnam site playing a major role in raising capacity for surface-treatment substrate transfer and Tazmo's own transfer equipment; semiconductor manufacturing equipment is running at full in-house utilisation, so collaboration with partner companies is most important, and more partners have been added from last year into this year; wet surface-treatment equipment capacity will come from the main production plant in Dongguan, China, and outsourcing.
